Thanks for the demo earlier today — useful session. A few quick follow ups from our side so we can prioritize internally: 

- Can you put together a concise recommended shortlist (2–3 models) for our use case (ED triage + discharge summary generation) with a short rationale focused on latency, token cost, and expected QA/regression risk?
- We need to see sample prompt sets and any benchmark results you ran (latency P50/P95 for our 512-token tails, and a quality proxy on our summary dataset is ideal).
- What are realistic cost ranges for 1M tokens/month at the pilot scale?

Also to flag: latency is a hard constraint for triage (P95 < 400ms target), while summaries can tolerate higher latency if quality is materially better.

Appreciate a short write-up and any artifacts we can share with engineering/security.

—Alex

Subject: Sequoia Health — recommended inference pathway and shortlists

Alex — thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a compact recommendation tailor-made to your two workloads (real-time triage + higher-quality discharge summaries). I’ve attached a prompt pack and the raw benchmark CSV.

Top-line recommended shortlist (2+1 fallback):

1) Redstone-7B-q4 (primary for triage)
- Why: Strong P50/P95 latency on A100/80GB for 512-token tails; continuous batching friendly; smaller memory footprint enables dense deployment across more GPUs.
- Latency: estimated P95 ~ 220–320ms with 1x concurrency and batching tuned to 16ms window (empirical on our pilot cluster).
- Cost: ~ $0.85–$1.10 per 1k-generation tokens (pilot estimate; depends on batching & cache hit rate).
- Quality tradeoff: Slightly lower abstractive fidelity vs large 13B+ models on nuanced summaries; very good for classification/triage.
- Risk: Medium — minor regression risk for complex clinical phrasing; recommend prompt engineering + golden prompt regression set.

2) Llama-13B-int8 (primary for summaries)
- Why: Best balance of quality/latency for long-form summaries in our tests — higher factuality and coherent structure without moving into 70B economics.
- Latency: P95 ~ 700–1,200ms (depends on sequence length and KV-cache reuse).
- Cost: ~ $1.90–$2.50 per 1k-generation tokens at pilot scale.
- Quality tradeoff: High — significantly fewer hallucinations on your summary sample compared to smaller models.
- Risk: Lower for quality, but higher infra cost and slightly more complex memory ops.

Fallback / capacity-saver: Halyon-70B-8bit variant (fallback for batch/off-peak high-quality generation)
- Use-case: Overnight batch processing of bulk summaries or when quality delta is critical and latency SLOs are relaxed.

Operational recommendations: 
- Start with a split pilot: Redstone-7B-q4 behind the triage route (default for live traffic) + Llama-13B-int8 for the summary route (can be warmed with prefix caching).
- Enable prefix/KV caching on common templates (discharge header + clinical context) to cut costs for summaries by ~15–25% in our tests.
- Canary rollout: 10% traffic to Llama-13B-int8 for summaries for 2 weeks with automatic rollback on quality regression alerts.

Artifacts attached: sequoia_prompt_pack_v1.json (prompt sets + evaluation prompts), sequoia_benchmarks_may2027.csv (latency/throughput runs across variants), sequoia_prototype_instructions.pdf (pilot infra + configs). Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SequoiaBenchmarks

Next steps I recommend: 
- You confirm whether triage must be P95 < 400ms hard SLO (we can propose dedicated capacity to reduce variance).
- If yes, we’ll prepare a pilot quote for dedicated pool + suggested canary schedule.
- We can run a short 48–72 hour regression run using your summary sample to produce an SRO (summary regression oracle) report.

Would you like me to draft the pilot commercial ballpark while Ben and Kim outline the infra/ops plan?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quick ops add from my side — thanks Sofia for the write-up. A few pragmatic notes to make the pilot low-friction: 

- Dedicated vs shared: For a hard P95 < 400ms for triage I recommend a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs depending on concurrency). Shared hosted can hit the numbers but has higher variance.
- Caching & batching: Use a 12–20ms batching window with request grouping by prompt shape. Enable prefix caching for the discharge header; for triage use a short KV cache TTL (few minutes).
- Safety/QA: Add a light hallucination filter (rerank by answer confidence + quick NER checks against clinical entities) in front of the generator for triage to avoid dangerous outputs.
- Monitoring: Instrument token-level cost, model route latency, and a prompt-set quality SLO (we’ll supply the eval harness).

I’ll prod infra to prepare a staging config and a quick runbook for getting the canary live. If legal/security need SOC 2 or DPA, loop Marissa and we’ll push those artifacts.

—Ben
Head of Solutions
